original.description: This procurement targets the delivery of the Copernicus Space Component acquisition services, including the Sentinels X-Band data acquisition operations and the S-band Telemetry, Tracking and Control (TTC) services.The X-Band Acquisition service aims at the on-ground reception of data sensed by the Sentinel satellites and the delivery of the acquired data in the form of CADU data stream for further ground segment operations. The TTC services aim at the reception of the satellite telecommands, their modulation and radiation to the satellite.Although covering different functions of the Copernicus Space Component (CSC) operations, the above-mentioned services may be considered rather similar in terms of required infrastructure and operations capabilities of the service providers. Accordingly the current procurement will include the possibility to cover both services.Building upon the operational experience gathered in the past years since the launch of Sentinel-1A in 2014, ESA intends to procure as much as possible standardized services using Contractors' owned state-of-the-art, off-the-shelf facilities and satellite-independent interfaces.In order to maximize the competition and the value for money for the to-be-procured services, the Services will be procured through the ESA Framework Agreements procedure, as established at Article 15 of ESA Procurement Regulations (ESA/REG/001, rev. 3 which can be downloaded at the following URL http://emits.sso.esa.int/emits/owa/emits.main). This procedure consists therefore in a two-step procurement approach, broken down as follows: Step 1 -Qualification Phase: The objective of this Step is to award, through an Open Competition Frame Contracts with the entities qualifying for the performance of the services subject of this procurement. Step 2 -Implementation Phase: The objective of this Step is to award, through Restricted Competitions between the Frame Contractors qualified under Step 1, the Work Orders allowing the performance of the procured services.An Information day about the subject procurement was organized at the European Space Agency (ESA) in December 2018. The location, date, registration process and Agenda of this briefing session was published on ESA Tendering website (EMITS) under "NEWS" (http://emits.sso.esa.int/emits/owa/emits.main). Potential bidders are invited to consult regularly ESA Tendering website (EMITS).The Acquisition And TTC Services For Copernicus procurements will be fundedby the Copernicus Programme and will be open exclusively to economic operators, which have their registered office in an EU Member State or Iceland or Norway.In order to access the Frame ITT Package from EMITS, any economic operator interested in the subject procurement will have to be registered as a potential ESA Tenderer. To register with ESA as a potential Tenderer, you will be requestedto complete the online questionnaire available ESA-STAR registration website: https://esastar-emr.sso.esa.int. While the registration process is underway, potential ESA Tenderers may access the Frame ITT Package through ESA's dedicated Copernicus server, which is accessible at: https://copernicus-emits.esa.int/

Introduction 

FuturEnergy Ireland is a leading Irish wind developer established in 2021 as a stand-alone joint venture between Coillte and ESB. The company was formed with an aim to maximise the potential of Ireland’s unique wind and land resources and accelerate Ireland’s transformation to a low carbon energy economy.  FuturEnergy Ireland is targeting the development of 1GW of renewable energy by 2030 through the advancement of high-quality onshore wind and battery storage projects. These projects would power an estimated 730,000 homes annually, make a significant contribution to Ireland’s commitment to produce 80% of electricity from renewable sources by the end of this decade, and deliver material emissions reductions.  


Contract for service – Invitation to tender

(a) Introduction
FuturEnergy Ireland is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced panel of Contractors to undertake LiDAR topographical survey services as required. The survey is
intended to provide accurate and reliable terrain, surface, imagery and survey-control data to support project development, design and related technical activities.
The successful Contractors will be responsible for all necessary planning, permissions, survey control, data acquisition, processing, independent validation, reporting and final deliverables.
Candidates should note that the objective of this tender competition is twofold: A) to appoint successful firms to the panel, and B) to award an initial assignment which relates to Project 1 located in Co Laois detailed in Appendix 5 of this document. 
Tenderers should note that four further projects are expected to be awarded through the panel shortly after it is established. These projects are not exhaustive, and additional projects will be awarded through the panel during its term, subject to project requirements and the Contracting Entity’s discretion.

(b) Objectives
The appointed Contractors shall:
Undertake a complete LiDAR high-resolution aerial imagery survey of the specified survey area.
Establish robust survey control and independent validation checkpoints using survey-grade GNSS RTK/PPK methods.
Provide accurate, quality-assured terrain, surface, point-cloud, imagery, contour and survey-control deliverables in the formats specified.
Demonstrate compliance with the required coordinate reference system, accuracy, point-density, validation and reporting requirements.

(c) Scope of Services




1. Survey Planning, Permissions and Mobilisation
The Contractors shall prepare the survey methodology and flight plan, secure all necessary permissions and approvals, coordinate access requirements, identify constraints and confirm the proposed survey programme before mobilisation.

2. Survey Control and Referencing
The survey shall be referenced to the Irish Transverse Mercator (ITM) coordinate system and Malin Head Ordnance Datum (MHOD). Ground control and independent validation checkpoints shall be established using survey-grade GNSS RTK/PPK methods.
A minimum of 20% of survey control points shall be retained as independent checkpoints and shall not be used during processing.


3. LiDAR and Aerial Imagery Acquisition
The Contractors shall acquire LiDAR and high-resolution aerial imagery sufficient to generate accurate Digital Terrain Models, Digital Surface Models, classified point clouds and orthorectified imagery.
The LiDAR system shall provide a minimum of five returns per pulse and shall be capable of reliable ground penetration through dense vegetation and forestry cover.

4. Minimum Technical Requirements
Horizontal accuracy: hard detail, including buildings, walls, roads and other defined features, shall be <= +/-50 mm; soft detail, including vegetation and natural terrain features, shall be <= +/-75 mm.
Vertical accuracy: hard detail and open ground shall be <= +/-75 mm; vegetated and forested areas shall be <= +/-100 mm.
Point density: minimum average LiDAR density of 150 points/m2 and minimum classified ground density of 15 points/m2 beneath forest canopy.
All reported accuracies shall be verified using independent checkpoints not used during processing.

5. Processing, Classification and Quality Assurance
The Contractors shall process, classify and validate the survey data, document the processing workflow, undertake appropriate quality assurance and quality control, and report achieved point density and horizontal and vertical accuracy.

6. Required Deliverables
Raw and classified LiDAR point clouds in LAS/LAZ format.
Digital Terrain Model (DTM) GeoTIFF at 0.25 m resolution.
Digital Surface Model (DSM) GeoTIFF at 0.25 m resolution.
Canopy Height Model (CHM) GeoTIFF at 0.5 m resolution
Orthorectified RGB imagery with a ground sampling distance of 5 cm/pixel or better.
0.5 m contour dataset in ESRI Shapefile and AutoCAD DWG formats. (Optional)
Survey control coordinates and validation results.
Final survey report detailing the survey methodology, equipment, processing workflow, point density, and horizontal and vertical accuracy assessment.




7. Optional Project Photography and Videography
The Contractors may be requested to carry out occasional aerial photography and videography surveys to capture site imagery for communications, publicity, stakeholder engagement, reporting and promotional purposes. All outputs shall be provided in high-resolution digital formats suitable for print and online use.

Deze raamovereenkomst heeft betrekking op de levering van landmeetkundige toestellen en bijhorende accessoires voor gebruik binnen de relevante opleidingen en praktijkomgevingen van Hogeschool Gent (HOGENT). Bestellingen gebeuren op afroep, naargelang de concrete behoeften van HOGENT. Binnen de raamovereenkomst kan HOGENT de in het bestek (artikel III.3) vermelde waterpastoestellen, manuele totaalstations, robotische totaalstations, GNSS-toestellen en bijhorende accessoires inclusief bijhorende toestelsoftware en licenties bestellen tegen de in de inventaris opgegeven forfaitaire eenheidsprijzen na korting. De bestellingen kunnen betrekking hebben op de aankoop van de betreffende toestellen en bijhorende accessoires, alsook sporadisch op de huur ervan voor beperkte periodes (week of maand). De raamovereenkomst omvat tevens de nodige platformsoftware met bijhorende licenties (eeuwigdurend licentierecht) voor het beheer, de verwerking, de analyse en de uitwisseling van meetgegevens. Ook kalibratie op afroep, opleiding en support maken deel uit van de opdracht. Daarnaast kan HOGENT tijdens de looptijd van de raamovereenkomst ook andere landmeetkundige toestellen en accessoires voor topografische metingen uit het productgamma van de opdrachtnemer bestellen die niet uitdrukkelijk in dit bestek zijn beschreven. De prijs ervan wordt bepaald op basis van de op het ogenblik van bestelling voor dat toestel geldende catalogusprijs/basisprijs, verminderd met het in de offerte opgegeven vaste globale kortingspercentage (en met de eventuele extra kortingen voor zover van toepassing).

description-proc.nld: Deze raamovereenkomst heeft betrekking op de levering van landmeetkundige toestellen en bijhorende accessoires voor gebruik binnen de relevante opleidingen en praktijkomgevingen van Hogeschool Gent (HOGENT). Bestellingen gebeuren op afroep, naargelang de concrete behoeften van HOGENT. Binnen de raamovereenkomst kan HOGENT de in het bestek (artikel III.3) vermelde waterpastoestellen, manuele totaalstations, robotische totaalstations, GNSS-toestellen en bijhorende accessoires inclusief bijhorende toestelsoftware en licenties bestellen tegen de in de inventaris opgegeven forfaitaire eenheidsprijzen na korting. De bestellingen kunnen betrekking hebben op de aankoop van de betreffende toestellen en bijhorende accessoires, alsook sporadisch op de huur ervan voor beperkte periodes (week of maand). De raamovereenkomst omvat tevens de nodige platformsoftware met bijhorende licenties (eeuwigdurend licentierecht) voor het beheer, de verwerking, de analyse en de uitwisseling van meetgegevens. Ook kalibratie op afroep, opleiding en support maken deel uit van de opdracht. Daarnaast kan HOGENT tijdens de looptijd van de raamovereenkomst ook andere landmeetkundige toestellen en accessoires voor topografische metingen uit het productgamma van de opdrachtnemer bestellen die niet uitdrukkelijk in dit bestek zijn beschreven. De prijs ervan wordt bepaald op basis van de op het ogenblik van bestelling voor dat toestel geldende catalogusprijs/basisprijs, verminderd met het in de offerte opgegeven vaste globale kortingspercentage (en met de eventuele extra kortingen voor zover van toepassing).
